From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: 2026-03-17T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redlines + subprocessors

Hi all — reviewed Acme's redlines. Summary and suggested responses below (high level first, then line items):

High-level responses:
- Subprocessors: current catalog includes a mix of cloud infra (managed GPUs), monitoring/observability providers, and S3-compatible storage providers. We publish a current list in our public subprocessor page and can provide a signed PDF snapshot for procurement.
- Transfers & safeguards: we rely on standard contractual safeguards and, where applicable, SCCs. We do not rely on any indemnity carve-outs beyond our standard DPA.
- Planned changes: none scheduled in the next 90 days; we will notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding any new subprocessor where legal/regulatory posture requires notice.

Proposed plain-language console blurb (2 options):
Option A (short): "Data processed by Redwood's Hosted API is routed to the region you select (US, EU, or APAC). We use vetted infrastructure partners and publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors in our Trust Center."
Option B (customer-facing, slightly longer): "When you choose a residency option in the console, requests and temporary model data are processed in the selected region. We use trusted cloud and monitoring partners — see our Trust Center for the current subprocessor list and details about data transfer safeguards."

Line-item redline comments: see attached console_plainlang_proposals_v1.docx for exact phrasing to align with your redlines. Key ask from legal: keep public language readable but do not promise immutability of subprocessor list; use "current as of" date where possible.

Happy to iterate — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
attachments: console_plainlang_proposals_v1.docx

Kimberly — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups:

- Will you provide a signed PDF snapshot of the current subprocessor list we can attach to the purchase order? That will speed procurement approval.
- DocuSign: yes please, send via DocuSign and copy procurement@acme-analytics.com on the final envelope.

If you can send the updated snippet + signed subprocessor snapshot by Thursday morning ET, we can route to procurement and finish contracting next week.

Thanks — Sara
